claims.text: Cryo-rolling followed by annealing can improve the strength-ductility combination of the eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Cryo-rolling and annealing can overcome brittleness and limited room-temperature tensile ductility in the starting material.
The untreated starting alloy has a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The applicable tensile-testing temperature is room temperature.
The applicable loading regime is quasi-static tension.
Cryo-rolling and annealing produce a hierarchical microstructure containing fine lamellar regions and ultrafine FCC grains.
The ultrafine FCC grains have an average size of approximately 200–250 nm.
The hierarchical microstructure contains soft, intermediate, and hard domains spanning a broad hardness range.
Profuse boundaries separate domains of different hardness in the treated microstructure.
Strain gradients between domains of different hardness generate significant back-stress strengthening.
Back-stress strengthening delays tensile necking and thereby improves both strength and ductility.
The intervention mitigates dislocation pile-ups, local stress concentrations, microcracking, and catastrophic damage at internal boundaries.
The treated alloy will exhibit simultaneous enhancement of strength and ductility relative to as-cast and cold-rolled-and-annealed material.
The treated alloy will have a yield strength greater than 1400 MPa.
The treated alloy will have elongation to failure greater than 14%.
As-cast and cold-rolled-and-annealed reference materials have an inferior strength-ductility combination because they lack nanoscale structural and hardness hierarchy.
The relationship between microstructure and mechanical properties in high-entropy alloys remains insufficiently understood.

contradictions.description: The initial state is already described as hierarchical, while essentially the same hierarchical structure is presented as the mediator created by cryo-rolling and annealing; the structural change caused by the intervention is therefore not clearly distinguished.
